title: Employment Agency employees hold one-hour strike across Bulgaria over wages

tea.why: Employees are protesting against low wages and the impact of high inflation on their purchasing power.
tea.want: A 350 euro wage increase, food vouchers, restoration of seniority bonuses, and the right to hold a second employment contract.
tea.changed: Nov 25: Employees across the country held a one-hour work stoppage to demand better pay and working conditions.

summary: On November 25, 2026, employees of the Employment Agency across Bulgaria participated in a one-hour strike to demand improved compensation and working conditions. Organised by the Podkrepa Confederation of Labour, the action involved staff stopping work for sixty minutes nationwide. Participants are calling for a 350 euro salary increase to offset inflation, the provision of food vouchers, and the reinstatement of seniority-based bonuses. Additionally, staff are seeking the right to hold secondary employment contracts to supplement their income. According to Kremina Atanasova, chair of the union branch, the protest aims to influence budget discussions between legislative readings, specifically criticising the disparity in proposed percentage-based wage increases. No official government response to the specific demands was reported in the provided sources.
demands: Right to hold a second employment contract
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: The Podkrepa Confederation of Labour announced a nationwide one-hour strike for the following day.
Employment Agency staff across Bulgaria conducted the one-hour work stoppage.
